reason: Two slices of armor-wear have landed. wear-zero-delay-shield at 8c55d3f brought W and canwearobj() whole; wear-delayed-suit at 5f91702 added Armor_on() and the delayed nomul(-oc_delay) fork, so W now wears both a shield and a suit and the delay arm is live rather than refused. Its correctness pass covers only the first slice, recorded through fc56134; the second is unreviewed and sits at 2 of 10 commits against the gate. All 24 entries are done (11), cannot-occur (10), later (2) or no-effect-yet (1) with evidence, and missingWorkByOwner is empty. The four remaining slots and the accessory half are refused above setworn(), so no excluded branch writes state, draws randomness or prints.

boundary.startingEvent: The hero types W, or #wear, at rhack()'s command dispatch, which js/cmd.js now admits and routes to do_wear.c dowear().
boundary.endingEvent: For a zero-delay piece, Shield_on() or Armor_on() has returned and on_msg() has printed 'You are now wearing ...'. For a delayed suit the boundary runs further: setworn() moves AC on the turn W is issued, nomul(-oc_delay) spends three or five helpless turns during which the pet moves and the counter advances, and the boundary ends when unmul() runs Armor_on() and prints 'You finish your dressing maneuver.' -- with no on_msg() line, which is the mirror image of T. An escaped prompt ends at ECMD_CANCEL, and a non-armor letter now ends at C's 'That is a silly thing to wear.' rather than at a refusal.
boundary.validInputs: W or #wear answered with a shield's or a suit's letter, with a non-armor or money letter, or escaped. 18 fresh segments in scripts/run-wear-armor.mjs cover them: the Valkyrie's shield taken off and put back, wizard-mode wished shields and suits that reach the *_on() callbacks with known still 0, Barbarian starts whose bimanual weapon drives canwearobj()'s shield refusal, a Caveman's leather armor at oc_delay 3 and a Samurai's splint mail at 5, a wished leather jacket at oc_delay 0, a food-ration letter and a money letter.
boundary.observables: The getobj() prompt's letter set, on_msg()'s wording, the status line's AC, the inventory window's '(being worn)' suffix and enchantment, the turn counter, and the random-number log, which must stay empty across this path: no branch inside the boundary draws.
boundary.exclusions: accessory_or_armor_on()'s armor == FALSE half, which the goal's boundary excludes so that doputon() stays unported; the four remaining slots, refused by the mask test above setworn(); Armor_on()'s dragon_armor_handling() and artifact_light() tails, refused by an Is_dragon_armor() guard hoisted above setworn() for the same reason; the Quest helm arm; retouch_object() for an artifact; remove_worn_item() for armor in a weapon slot; and flags.verbose off, which still has no end-to-end case.

candidateListMethod.upstreamEntryPoints: do_wear.c dowear() 2432-2452 and its whole call tree: wear_ok() 3463-3469 over equip_ok() 3402-3447, accessory_or_armor_on() 2209-2431, canwearobj() 2030-2208, already_wearing() 2011-2014, on_msg() 76-105 and Shield_on() 705-732. The second slice adds Armor_on() 886-906 and invent.c silly_thing() 2093-2131, the latter reached from getobj() rather than from do_wear.c.
candidateListMethod.dispatchTablesAndCatalogs: objects.h's nine SHIELD rows 653-679, read for oc_delay, which is 0 for every one of them; the ARMOR macro at 418-427, whose BITS passes uskn 1 for every armor row, which is why u_init.c:1215 marks a starting shield known; and js/cmd.js's ADMITTED_COMMANDS and the extended-command ef_funct switch, the two tables that decide whether W is reachable at all. objects.h's suit rows were read the same way for oc_delay: leather armor 3, splint mail 5, dwarvish mithril-coat 1 and leather jacket 0, which is the one suit taking the immediate arm.
candidateListMethod.reachableHelpers: Every call inside dowear()'s tree was followed to a ported owner or a named refusal. The pure obj.h and mondata.h macros canwearobj() needs -- is_helmet, is_boots, is_gloves, is_cloak, is_shirt, is_suit, is_sword, WrappingAllowed, cantweararm, has_horns -- arrived as one bulk batch under AGENTS.md's pure-function rule, and objnam.c obj_is_pname() replaced the inline refusal yname() carried.
candidateListMethod.javascriptCrossCheck: grep -n '^export function|^export async function|^function|^async function' js/do_wear.js enumerated the file's 33 owners; git show --stat 8c55d3f listed the ten files the slice touched; npm run quality -- slice-mutants --range a2189e1..8c55d3f confirmed the Mutants trailer; and npm run checkpoint at 8c55d3f reported the suite, the seven generated-data checks and the development score together. For the second slice, git show --stat 5f91702 listed seven files, npm run quality -- slice-mutants --range 6d42af2..5f91702 confirmed the trailer, and npm run checkpoint at 5f91702 reported the suite, the generated-data checks and an unchanged development score.
candidateListMethod.remainingLimits: Two. The list is built from do_wear.c's static call tree, so a caller reaching these functions from outside that file would not appear in it; js/invent.js getobj() is the one such caller and its callback contract changed in this slice, which is why the entry below names it. And flags.verbose off is unexercised end to end, so on_msg()'s silent arm rests on a direct unit call rather than on a recorded frame. A third limit now applies: the mutation run over the second slice produced only three sites, so most of its diff carries no mutable operator and the eleven hand-broken lines recorded in its commit body are what stands in for that coverage.

sourceReview: Every branch and helper reachable from dowear() through Shield_on()'s return was traced against nethack-c/upstream/src/do_wear.c at commit 16ff591, covering state writes and random-number order. The path draws no random number at any point, which the 12 fresh cases confirm at 30,539 recorded calls, all matching. canwearobj() was read whole because C's whole-function rule and its single *mask consumer force it to land intact, and each of its seven slot arms was classified above. Stops, partial implementations and absences are identified individually: seven UnsupportedWearError refusals, all placed above setworn() so that no excluded branch writes state, draws randomness or prints; one deliberate non-write, gw.wasinwater, with its reason at the site; one field with no JavaScript home, svc.context.takeoff.what; and one shared contract change, getobj()'s callback signature, whose reach beyond do_wear.c is recorded as a limit of this list. Two mutants survive with reasons in the commit body: js/cmd.js's state.multi < 0, which only chooses whether to clear an always-empty command queue and which seven sibling rhack() arms carry identically, and js/do_wear.js's fingers_or_gloves(false), whose two answers coincide because the arm above it has already returned for a filled glove slot -- the reason C passes FALSE at do_wear.c:2153.
